strategy: Run offline parser scripts/hermes_systemd_recovery_fixture.py against the failure fixture to confirm the failure shape (no systemctl, no journalctl, no env scan).
Inspect parsed JSON: confirm service_failed=true, missing_env_var=MODEL_PROVIDER (or expected env), expected_port set, port_not_listening=true, dropin_env_misconfigured=true.
Recommend deterministic check order: systemctl --user status, journalctl --user -u, systemctl --user show-environment, drop-in Environment lines, expected port, Telegram smoke.
Never print or persist secrets, API keys, tokens, cookies, or Authorization headers in any recovery step.
Never restart the real hermes-gateway.service from a recipe script; always have a human run the recovery commands on the real host.
Re-run the parser + inspect/validate/apply tool chain after each fixture or Gene change; never bypass the validators.
summary: Hermes systemd user-service recovery: offline fixture parser identifies service_failed / missing_env_var / expected_port / dropin_env_misconfigured shape; recommends deterministic systemctl + journalctl + show-environment + drop-in + port + Telegram smoke check order; never reads .env, never restarts the real service, never persists secrets. Includes both qualified (systemd_failure:user-service) and bare (systemd_failure) signal forms for evolver scanner normalization.
